pages.title: How Salesmsg
pages.subtitle: Exactly how credits are calculated for every message — so your balance never surprises you.

rows.definition: Every letter, number, space and symbol in your message counts.
Standard text character set — A–Z, 0–9 and common punctuation. Fits 160 characters per segment.
Expanded set for emojis, accented letters and non-Latin scripts. Fits only 70 characters per segment.
One billed unit of a text. Long messages split into segments automatically by the carrier.
The unit deducted from your balance. One segment = one credit.

blocks.title: One emoji switches the whole message
blocks.text: A single emoji or accented character anywhere switches the entire message to Unicode — not just the part after it. A short message can cost 2 credits.

pages.title: What everything
pages.subtitle: Every activity deducts credits — inbound messages cost the same as outbound.

rows.label: SMS
rows.note: Inbound and outbound; 160 chars/segment plain text, 70 with emojis.

rows.label: RCS
rows.note: Same as MMS, including international. Failed RCS messages are still charged.

rows.label: Calling
rows.note: Standard U.S.: 1/min. Toll-free and international cost more — see rates.

rows.label: Call forwarding
rows.note: Charged from when ringing starts, whether answered or not.

rows.label: Transcription
rows.note: Applies to calls and voicemails, including the AI summary.

rows.label: AI agent messages
rows.note: On top of the normal SMS, MMS or RCS cost.

blocks.title: Calling and international rates vary
blocks.text: Toll-free inbound: 3 credits/min. Alaska (907) is 5 credits/min outbound. International rates vary by country — Salesmsg covers 236 countries. Full rate list in the Help Center.

blocks.title: Credits aren't carrier fees
blocks.text: Carriers add their own per-message surcharges; 10DLC registration has its own fees. Both appear as separate invoice lines — not deducted from your credit balance.

pages.title: Your balance and
pages.subtitle: What rolls over, what stops at zero, and how credits add up in practice.

rows.definition: Reset on your billing anniversary. Annual credits granted in full on the renewal date.
Roll over — auto-recharge top-ups and one-off purchases stay until you spend them.
Messages and calls stop until you top up. Set up auto-recharge to stay online.
Contacts can still text you, taking your balance negative. Shortfall deducted from your next purchase.
Salesmsg checks your balance first and prompts you to top up before sending.

blocks.heading: Worked examples
blocks.footnote: The carrier splits long messages into segments; the recipient sees them as one. Credits are based on actual segments transmitted, which the composer shows before you send.

pages.title: Tips and
pages.subtitle: Simple habits to save credits plus answers to the most common billing questions.

paragraphs.text: Stay under 160 characters. Skip emojis — one drops the limit to 70. Curly quotes and em dashes switch to Unicode too.
The composer shows segment count before you send — check on broadcasts and templates. Paste as plain text to avoid hidden characters from Word or Docs.

rows.label: A failed RCS message
rows.note: RCS is billed on the attempt, including fallbacks to SMS/MMS.

items.question: Why did a short message cost 2 credits?
items.answer: A Unicode character — an emoji, accented letter, or curly quote — switched the whole message to a 70-character limit.

items.question: Do contacts' replies cost us credits?
items.answer: Yes. Inbound messages bill at the same rate as outbound, and keep arriving even when your balance hits zero.

items.question: Do unused credits carry forward?
items.answer: Plan credits reset each billing period. Auto-recharge top-ups and other separately purchased credits roll over until spent.
